title: Trump says Iran probably responsible for attack on Saudi pipeline
gist: Trump said Iran is probably responsible for the aerial attack that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the kingdom's main crude export route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, and revealed that Yemen's Houthis had phoned his administration asking the US to stay out of the conflict while letting most ships pass.

insights.claim: US President Donald Trump publicly attributed the aerial attack that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline to Iran, saying 'I think they are, probably they are' when asked about Iranian responsibility.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Presidential attribution to Iran rather than to the Houthis raises the probability of direct US-Iran retaliation and a wider risk premium on Gulf energy assets.
insights.quote: I think they are, probably they are
insights.locator: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday

insights.claim: Trump said he had spoken with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and described him as a 'good friend', signaling Washington is coordinating with Riyadh on the response.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Direct Trump-MBS contact after a strike on Saudi export infrastructure is the channel through which any US military involvement would be negotiated.
insights.locator: The U.S. president also said that he had spoken

insights.claim: The East-West pipeline that was shut by the attack is one of Saudi Arabia's main routes for exporting crude while bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Knocking out the Hormuz workaround removes the principal physical hedge against a strait closure, so Saudi export capacity becomes hostage to Hormuz itself.
insights.locator: one of the kingdom's main routes for exporting crude

insights.claim: Satellite imagery from Planet Labs documented damage to the East-West pipeline facility in the Hejaz region, giving independent confirmation of physical damage rather than claimed damage.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Independent satellite verification means the supply disruption is real and can be tracked by commercial imagery, a faster signal than official Saudi statements.
insights.locator: Satellite image shows damage to the East-West pipeline facility

insights.claim: Trump said Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis called his administration to indicate they did not want the United States to become directly involved in the conflict.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A direct Houthi-Washington back channel implies the group is calibrating attacks to avoid triggering US entry, which caps but does not eliminate escalation.
insights.locator: Trump added that Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis had called his admnistration

insights.claim: Trump characterized Houthi behavior toward shipping as selective, saying they are letting most ships go through with only one country's vessels targeted.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Selective rather than blanket targeting means Red Sea freight and insurance rates should differentiate sharply by flag and ownership rather than move as one.
insights.quote: They would much prefer not having us involved, and they're letting most ships go through.
insights.locator: "They would much prefer not having us involved"
